version: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0

controls.title: Ensure that Microsoft Defender for Servers is set to 'On'
controls.description: The Defender for Cloud servers plan must be enabled on every subscription in scope.
controls.rationale: Without the servers plan there is no endpoint detection, no vulnerability assessment and no just-in-time access on Azure VMs.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Enabling the plan incurs a per-server monthly charge.
controls.nistCategory: DE.CM-01 Networks and network services are monitored
controls.remediationProcedure: PUT the pricing resource with properties.pricingTier set to Standard.

audit.name: Read the Defender for Servers pricing tier

assertions.failure: Microsoft Defender for Servers is on the {actual} tier; CIS requires {expected}.
assertions.hint: Set the VirtualMachines pricing tier to Standard on every in-scope subscription.

rollback.name: Restore the previous Defender pricing tier

controls.title: Ensure that 'Secure transfer required' is set to 'Enabled'
controls.description: Every storage account must reject unencrypted HTTP requests.
controls.rationale: Without secure transfer, blob and file traffic including the shared key can traverse the network in clear text.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Clients using http:// endpoints will need to move to https://.
controls.auditProcedure:
GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts?api-version=2023-01-01
Confirm every account has properties.supportsHttpsTrafficOnly set to true.
controls.remediationProcedure: PATCH each storage account setting properties.supportsHttpsTrafficOnly to true.

audit.name: List storage accounts allowing plain HTTP

assertions.failure: Not every storage account requires secure transfer ({actual} across {count} accounts).
assertions.hint: Set supportsHttpsTrafficOnly to true on each storage account that is still accepting HTTP.

remediation.name: Require secure transfer on all storage accounts

rollback.name: Restore the previous storage transport settings

controls.title: Ensure that 'Public access level' is disabled for storage accounts with blob containers
controls.description: Anonymous blob public access must be turned off at the storage account level.
controls.rationale: A public container is the single most common cause of accidental cloud data exposure.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Anything relying on anonymous blob reads will break and must move to SAS or managed identity.
controls.auditProcedure:
GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts?api-version=2023-01-01
Confirm properties.allowBlobPublicAccess is false for every account.
controls.remediationProcedure: PATCH each storage account setting properties.allowBlobPublicAccess to false.

audit.name: List storage accounts allowing public blob access

assertions.failure: Anonymous blob access is still permitted ({actual} across {count} storage accounts).
assertions.hint: Set allowBlobPublicAccess to false on every storage account, then re-issue SAS tokens for any legitimate anonymous consumer.

controls.title: Ensure the 'Minimum TLS version' for storage accounts is set to 'Version 1.2'
controls.description: Storage accounts must reject TLS versions below 1.2.
controls.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known weaknesses and are no longer acceptable for regulated data in transit.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Very old clients that cannot negotiate TLS 1.2 will fail to connect.
controls.auditProcedure: GET the storage accounts and confirm properties.minimumTlsVersion is TLS1_2.
controls.remediationProcedure: PATCH each storage account setting properties.minimumTlsVersion to TLS1_2.

audit.name: Read the minimum TLS version of every storage account

assertions.failure: Not every storage account enforces TLS 1.2 ({actual}).
assertions.hint: Set minimumTlsVersion to TLS1_2 on each storage account.

controls.title: Ensure that RDP access from the Internet is evaluated and restricted
controls.description: No network security group rule may allow inbound TCP 3389 from the Internet.
controls.rationale: Internet-facing RDP is scanned continuously and is the most common initial access vector for ransomware in Azure.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Administrators must reach the VM through Bastion, a VPN or just-in-time access instead.
controls.nistCategory: PR.IR-01 Networks and environments are protected
controls.auditProcedure:
GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups?api-version=2023-05-01
Confirm no security rule allows destinationPortRange 3389 from source * or Internet.
controls.remediationProcedure: Change the offending rule's access to Deny, or narrow its source to a specific address prefix, then adopt Azure Bastion or just-in-time VM access.

audit.name: Find NSG rules exposing RDP to the Internet

assertions.failure: These network security group rules expose RDP (TCP 3389) to the Internet: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Set the rule access to Deny or scope its source prefix to the corporate range, and reach the VMs through Azure Bastion instead.

remediation.name: Deny inbound RDP from the Internet

rollback.name: Restore the previous NSG rule state

controls.title: Ensure that SSH access from the Internet is evaluated and restricted
controls.description: No network security group rule may allow inbound TCP 22 from the Internet.
controls.rationale: Exposed SSH is brute-forced continuously and gives direct shell access when a key or password is weak.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Administrators must reach Linux VMs through Bastion, a VPN or just-in-time access.
controls.nistCategory: PR.IR-01 Networks and environments are protected
controls.auditProcedure: GET the network security groups and confirm no rule allows destinationPortRange 22 from source * or Internet.
controls.remediationProcedure: Set the offending rule's access to Deny or narrow its source prefix.

audit.name: Find NSG rules exposing SSH to the Internet

assertions.failure: These network security group rules expose SSH (TCP 22) to the Internet: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Set the rule access to Deny or scope its source prefix, and use Azure Bastion for administrative access.

remediation.name: Deny inbound SSH from the Internet

controls.title: Ensure that a 'Diagnostic Setting' exists for the subscription activity log
controls.description: The subscription activity log must be exported to a Log Analytics workspace or storage account.
controls.rationale: The activity log is retained for only 90 days by default, which is shorter than most breach detection windows.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Log export incurs ingestion and retention charges.
controls.nistCategory: DE.AE-03 Information is correlated from multiple sources
controls.auditProcedure:
GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/providers/Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2021-05-01-preview
Confirm at least one setting exists and is enabled.
controls.remediationProcedure: Create a diagnostic setting for the subscription activity log targeting a Log Analytics workspace with at least 365 days of retention.

assertions.failure: No diagnostic setting exports the subscription activity log ({count} found).
assertions.hint: Create a diagnostic setting sending the activity log to a Log Analytics workspace with 365-day retention.

remediation.name: Export the activity log to Log Analytics

controls.title: Ensure Web App redirects all HTTP traffic to HTTPS
controls.description: Every App Service must have HTTPS Only enabled.
controls.rationale: Without the redirect, session cookies and bearer tokens can be captured on the first plaintext request.
controls.userImpact: Impact: HTTP callers are redirected; clients pinned to http:// need updating.
controls.auditProcedure:
GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites?api-version=2022-03-01
Confirm properties.httpsOnly is true for every site.
controls.remediationProcedure: PATCH each site setting properties.httpsOnly to true.

audit.name: List App Services accepting plain HTTP

assertions.failure: Not every App Service enforces HTTPS ({actual} across {count} sites).
assertions.hint: Set httpsOnly to true on each App Service still accepting plain HTTP.

remediation.name: Enforce HTTPS on all App Services

rollback.name: Restore the previous App Service transport settings

controls.title: Ensure that the expiration date is set on all keys and secrets
controls.description: Key Vault keys and secrets must carry an expiry date.
controls.rationale: Secrets without an expiry live forever, which defeats rotation and leaves leaked material valid indefinitely.
controls.userImpact: Impact: Applications must handle rotation before the expiry date.
controls.auditProcedure: Enumerate each Key Vault's keys and secrets and confirm attributes.exp is set.
controls.remediationProcedure: Set an expiry on every key and secret, then adopt an automated rotation policy.

audit.name: Find Key Vault objects with no expiry

assertions.failure: These Key Vault objects have no expiry date: {actual}.
assertions.hint: Set an expiry on each key and secret and configure an automated rotation policy.
